title: Adaptive Action Framing & SDK Workbench PRD (draft)
content:
Overview:

This document sketches a pragmatic PRD for an "adaptive action framing" feature set and accompanying SDK workbench intended to improve developer ergonomics for streaming responses, tool invocations, and structured outputs. It is intentionally exploratory: the focus is on a small, testable surface that lets client SDKs negotiate fidelity and action boundaries dynamically while the hosted runtime optimizes latency/cost tradeoffs.

Goals (high-level):
- Make tool-calls and structured outputs robust in lossy/partial-stream contexts (mobile/edge)
- Give SDKs an ergonomic surface to express progressive fidelity requirements (e.g., quick summary vs. full action)
- Provide an incremental rollout path so backend runtime improvements (caching, batching) can be validated without breaking clients
- Preserve clear observability for developers (per-action latency/cost, partial vs final semantics)

Problem statement:
- Current streaming model returns incremental text blobs. Tool calls embedded in streams either arrive late or require heavyweight client-side parsing.
- SDKs are forced to either (a) buffer until final response (bad UX), or (b) attempt brittle heuristics to detect action frames (error-prone).
- Mobile clients need smaller, earlier frames for acceptable perceived latency; server-side batching/quantization mustn't silently change semantics.

Proposal summary:
- Introduce an "Action Frame" primitive in the streamed protocol: discrete frames with explicit types (prompt-suggestion, action-invocation, partial-schema, commit). Frames are explicit JSON-ish chunks with a lightweight header for quick client parsing.
- Add "fidelity hints" to client invocation: clients declare fidelity ladder (fast/medium/accurate) and per-call tolerance for partial schemas. Server will try to honor ladder for the earliest frames and progressively fill details.
- SDK Workbench: new reference client SDK components and test harness that let product and partners author "action composers"—declarative maps from frames -> UI/update behavior. The workbench will ship with sample adapters (web, iOS) and a test harness simulating flaky networks.

Streaming frame sketch (informal):
- Each stream delta is one of: TEXT, FRAME_HEADER, FRAME_PAYLOAD, FRAME_COMMIT, HEARTBEAT.
- FRAME_HEADER: {frame_id, frame_type, fidelity_hint, schema_id?, partial:bool} (small header only)
- FRAME_PAYLOAD: payload chunk for frame_id (can be multiple payload chunks)
- FRAME_COMMIT: marks finality for frame_id; server attaches token-cost and model-version metadata on commit

Example (pseudo-stream sequence):
- HEADER(frame-42, action-invocation, fidelity=fast)
- PAYLOAD(chunk1)  // quick directive + tool name
- HEADER(frame-43, partial-schema, fidelity=fast)
- PAYLOAD(schema snippet)
- COMMIT(frame-42)  // client can call tool immediately with minimal params
- PAYLOAD(schema completion)
- COMMIT(frame-43)  // full schema available later

Tool calling semantics:
- Tools are first-class frames. A tool invocation may be executed by the client after either: (a) an explicit COMMIT(frame, allow_partial=true), or (b) a COMMIT after server notifies partial allowed and client opted in.
- Server must include fallback suggestions: if partial invocation fails client-side, server attempt to synthesize a safe no-op or rollback instruction in the stream.
- Tool-call observability: every tool frame includes an invocation_id (correlates to logs), latency_buckets, and an optional recommended_retry_strategy.

Structured output & schema negotiation:
- Schemas are versioned small JSON-schemas discovered via schema_id. Server may stream a partial schema ID + brief preview.
- Clients declare acceptable schema_versions at call time; server returns decisions whether it can honor exact schema or will return an adapter mapping (server-synthesized compatibility layer).
- For backwards compatibility, free-form TEXT frames remain supported; structured frames are a co-existence layer.

SDK ergonomics (workbench priorities):
- Minimal surface: one new client method generateStream({prompt, fidelityLadder, schemaPreferences, onFrame}) where onFrame receives parsed frame headers and payloads.
- Helpers: actionComposer utilities to map frame_type -> default behavior (renderPartial, queToolCall, presentConfirmation).
- Fallback patterns: SDK exposes small primitives for safe execution: allowPartialExecute(tool, frame) returns a promise that resolves to toolResult or a clientError object; SDK includes default UI modal for confirmation flows.

Example SDK snippet (JS pseudo):
- const stream = client.generateStream({prompt, fidelityLadder:["fast","accurate"], schemaPreferences:["order-v2"]});
- stream.onFrame((header,payload) => {
-   if (header.type === 'action-invocation') actionComposer.queue(header, payload);
-   if (header.type === 'partial-schema') schemaStore.patch(header.schema_id,payload);
- });

Operational constraints / compatibility:
- Frame headers should be <512 bytes to make parsing cheap.
- Server guarantees: COMMIT frame will eventually appear for each action frame unless a terminal error is emitted.
- Cost accounting: partial frames count tokens as they are emitted. COMMIT includes a token_summary for charge estimation.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0: internal SDK workbench + runtime integration tests (no public surface) — validate header size, partial commit behavior, and fallback generation.
- Phase 1: opt-in beta API flag for select customers. SDK workbench distributed as beta packages. Collect per-frame metrics and developer feedback.
- Phase 2: GA for hosted API: default on for new model endpoints, backward compat flag for older clients.

Success metrics:
- Developer experience: 75% fewer bug reports related to tool-call ordering from beta customers in 8 weeks.
- Latency: 50% reduction in time-to-first-action-frame for fast fidelity tier vs baseline.
- Cost: no more than 10% token cost overhead vs current streaming for equivalent work; measured by token_summary samples.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Authorization model for tool frames: should the server attach signed tool descriptors so clients can verify integrity? (security team consult required)
- Partial commit safety: define concrete rollback semantics and when server provides best-effort compensating actions.
- How to version schema_ids and guarantee deterministic upcasts/downcasts across runtime upgrades? Need spec for adapters.
- UX experiments: default client behavior for partial invokes (auto-execute vs confirm) — test in workbench.

Appendix: quick test cases to implement in workbench harness:
- Flaky network: server emits header+payload, long gap, commit arrives; client must surface "optimistic action" UI and allow cancellation.
- Schema mismatch: client requests order-v3 but server cannot produce v3; server streams adapter mapping -> client must detect and surface warning.
- Tool failure: client executes partial invocation and tool returns error; server should emit compensating frame in same session.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive at the wire-level to reduce ambiguity for SDK implementers. Feedback requested on header field set, commit guarantees, and cost-accounting model.
- Priority: get a minimal internal demo in 6 weeks.

Unresolved: need cross-team working session with Security, SDK, and Serving Runtime to align on signature format, token accounting, and canary gating for Dedicated customers.
